clue.text: Day directly after the rains

indicators.note: after places the second word straight behind the day's short form

parts.note: Mon is the usual short form of Monday
directly in its older sense means very shortly, without delay

explanation.surface: A weather report saying it will be dry the very day after the rainy season ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The monsoon is the seasonal wind that brings South Asia its heavy summer downpours.

clue.text: The staff of Mother Church

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A question about who works for the mother church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The staff' looks like the employees of the church; it is a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of authority, as in Parliament, is called this.

clue.text: Where Catherine Morland is bearing a baby with lots of energy

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Where Catherine Morland is bearing a baby with lots of energy (10,5)'. NORTH (bearing) is clear, but ANGERABBEY needs an anagram of A BABY + ENERG(y) and no clue word is left to signal it except 'with lots of energy', which would do two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Where Catherine Morland is bearing a baby with lots of energy

clue.text: Hardly plumb stupid

definitions.meaning: an angle wider than a right angle is far from vertical or square

explanation.definitionFit: An obtuse angle exceeds ninety degrees, so it is not plumb; figuratively the word means dull-witted.

clue.text: Original song heard (and seen once) at the Windmill

indicators.note: heard says the phrase is to be spoken and the sound written down

parts.note: a fresh song is a new ditty

explanation.surface: Recalling a fresh number performed at a famous old London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Windmill Theatre in London's Soho was famous from the 1930s to the 1960s for its motionless nude tableaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed performers were the Windmill Theatre's notorious attraction, hence nakedness was what audiences saw there.

clue.text: Oasis emerged herein as tribe out East mixed soft drink

indicators.note: mixed says the remaining letters of the word tribe are jumbled
out says a letter is dropped from the word tribe

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
pop is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Travel writing about a desert spring where a tribe from the East shared a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from TRIBE, and 'mixed' shuffles the remaining TRIB into BRIT. 'Oasis' looks like a desert spring but is the 1990s Manchester band.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis were one of the leading bands of the mid-1990s British guitar-pop movement.

clue.text: 'Arry's sonar location system

parts.note: a dropped-aitch Cockney is by tradition born within earshot of a particular church's peal, so that ringing locates him like sonar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry with the dropped H marks a Cockney; tradition says a true Cockney is born within hearing of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow Bells define Cockney territory: being born within their sound is what makes a Londoner a Cockney.

clue.text: Attention that's paid to uncle

definitions.meaning: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, who charges a fee on money lent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest means close attention, and it is also the charge paid on a loan such as a pawnbroker's.

clue.text: The shareholder's portion

parts.note: read 'share' as a ploughshare, so its holder is the farmhand steering the plough, and his portion is the meal he eats

explanation.walkthrough: A ploughshare is the blade of a plough; the pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle is named after the man who holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bread-cheese-and-pickle pub meal is named for the farm worker, the one who holds the ploughshare.

clue.text: Get check, give a tip

definitions.meaning: to fix a point or cap on the end of something

explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to finish it off; literally, fixing a tip means attaching a final piece.

clue.text: One laden with gold having sound incentive

indicators.note: sound says the word for incentive is spoken and its sound written

parts.note: a carrot is a reward dangled as an incentive

explanation.surface: Someone loaded with gold and with a good reason to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit measuring gold's purity: 24 of them means the metal is pure gold.

clue.text: Work less; give it up!

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
less as a preposition means without

explanation.surface: Telling someone to stop working so hard and quit altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to manage in its absence, giving it up.

clue.text: Get horse on your chest, might get strong headache!

definitions.text: Get horse on your chest, might get strong headache!

parts.words: Get horse on your chest, might get strong headache!
parts.note: 'horse' is slang for heroin, so taking it brings on a heavy head; the chest picture suggests pursuing a fire-breathing beast tattooed there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is slang for heroin; the phrase means inhaling heated heroin fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means smoking heroin by inhaling the vapour from a heated foil, a drug-user's slang phrase.

clue.text: Told how rotten clue I formed was pass

indicators.note: rotten says the letters of clue and I are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: was passé, out of fashion, means dated

explanation.surface: A complaint that a badly made clue was out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' shuffles CLUEI into ELUCI; 'formed' links that to DATED, read as 'was passé'.
explanation.definitionFit: Explaining how something works is making it clear, which is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Go-between shedding light on things

definitions.meaning: an old flaming torch carried through dark streets

explanation.walkthrough: A link was a torch of pitch and tow carried by link-boys to light the way in old London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A connector joins two parties; the same word once meant a street torch giving light.

clue.text: He fired Tom Brown with enthusiasm!

definitions.text: He fired Tom Brown with enthusiasm!

parts.words: He fired Tom Brown with enthusiasm!
parts.note: read 'fired' literally: the Rugby School bully gleefully roasted the hero of Tom Brown's Schooldays in front of a fire

explanation.walkthrough: In Tom Brown's Schooldays the bully of Rugby School roasts Tom against the fire; 'fired with enthusiasm' pretends to mean inspired.
explanation.definitionFit: The bully of Rugby School in the novel tormented Tom Brown by holding him before the fire.

clue.text: Malarky, you say, could be going over the rabbi's head

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: you said aloud sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing as nonsense what goes over a rabbi's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MALARKY plus U into the Jewish skullcap; 'going over the head' pretends to mean beyond understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: This skullcap is worn on top of the head by Jewish men, a rabbi among them.

clue.text: Stiles, Law and Charlton hooked up again on side?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
United, here Manchester United, is a football side

explanation.surface: Asks whether three football legends have joined forces again in a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Bobby Charlton played together for Manchester United in the 1960s, which points the solver to the team name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together once more, brought back into union after a separation.

clue.text: Spaer, a sea captain, returned from this port

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the port's name is taken out of the run of words about the captain

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sea captain named Spaer sailed back from some harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters AERASEAC sit inside 'Spaer, a sea captain'; 'returned' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesarea is an ancient harbour city on the coast of Israel, so it is a port.

clue.text: Bird's airspeed indicator

definitions.meaning: a small wading shorebird of the sandpiper family
a unit of speed of one nautical mile per hour, used for aircraft and ships

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sandpiper-like wader and the nautical-mile-per-hour unit used for aircraft speed.

clue.text: Veil over fabulous bird, had to penetrate

indicators.note: to penetrate says the word had goes inside the reversed bird
over in a down clue says the bird's name is turned upside down

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A veil drawn over a legendary bird that had to be pierced.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights; in a down clue 'over' turns it upside down, and 'to penetrate' sends 'had' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chador is a full-length cloak and veil worn by some Muslim women, especially in Iran.

clue.text: A German mine defused at Bletchley Park

indicators.note: defused says the mine is taken apart and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Wartime bomb disposal at the British codebreaking centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Bletchley Park in Buckinghamshire was Britain's wartime codebreaking centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bletchley Park is famous for cracking this German cipher machine during the Second World War.

clue.text: One makes emergency stop as dodgy dames lend a hand

indicators.note: dodgy, meaning dubious or unsound, says the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shady ladies helping out when a vehicle has to brake suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges DAMES LEND A HAND into the safety device.
explanation.definitionFit: A train driver's safety control that stops the train automatically if the driver lets go of it.

clue.text: Resistance to Dame Edna?

definitions.meaning: a force holding back motion, as air resists a moving car
Barry Humphries's character was performed by a man dressed as a woman

explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage was the comic character of the Australian Barry Humphries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means resistance to motion and also a man's female costume, as worn for Dame Edna.

clue.text: Classified prohibition overdue with onset of drunkenness

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a prohibition
something overdue is late

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of drunkenness is taken

explanation.surface: A ban arriving late, once drinking has begun, is kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified in the sense of sorted and arranged into tables or categories.

clue.text: King's daughter the Italian abandoned: no hope for him!

indicators.note: abandoned says the Italian article is left out of the daughter's name

parts.note: Goneril is a daughter of Shakespeare's King Lear
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A princess abandoned by her Italian lover, and he is beyond help.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IL from GONERIL; 'the Italian' is IL, Italian for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond hope is doomed, a person as good as dead.

clue.text: Seaman's goal in Prohibition America?

definitions.meaning: the shore a sailor longs to reach
the US under Prohibition was alcohol-free, a 'dry' country

explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is what a sailor longs for, and a country banning drink is jokingly 'dry'.

clue.text: Motorist with hood flapping and rag out

indicators.note: flapping says the letters of hood and rag flutter into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver going along with the car hood loose and a rag hanging out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' rearranges HOOD and RAG; 'out' only adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish, reckless driver, so the word is a particular kind of motorist.
